findings.how: plutil is now parsed instead of taking the last argument as the file. The parser skips each command's own values: -insert/-replace take key, type and value (no value for -array/-dictionary); -remove a key; -create/-convert a format; -extract a key and format; -type a key. It also skips the values of -o, -e and -expect. -s, -r, -n and -append are flags wherever they appear. Every other argument, and everything after --, is a file. Files are writes for -insert, -replace, -remove, -create and -convert without -o, and for an unresolved command; otherwise they are read through readArgs.

findings.how: Each row that skipped a read file now judges it as a read. date -f/--file is judged on GNU systems only, because BSD date's -f is a format string; an unseen value asks. du now judges -X, --exclude-from and --files0-from, and --exclude stays a pattern. tree --fromfile now judges its operands as files read, and find -files0-from judges its file. A new pass, optionPaths(), runs after every program's own row. It judges any long option named like a file to read (--file, --*-file, --*files, --files0-from, --*-from, but not --profile) as a read, in both the --x=v and --x v forms, and asks when the value can't be seen. It skips text programs and programs whose arguments name files elsewhere (ssh, docker, podman, kubectl), and it skips stdin, null sinks and URLs. This also closes git add/rm/reset --pathspec-from-file and gh --body-file. tar -T/-X was already fixed in step A (63b2657). sort and wc --files0-from already asked, and fixtures now cover them. One deliberate side effect: node --env-file=.env now asks, as source .env and node app.js .env already did. | repair: Added SETTINGS_FILE_OPTION = {defaults-file, defaults-extra-file}. optionPaths skips these options unless the program is my_print_defaults or --print-defaults is given, because those print what the file holds. --env-file still asks for node, bun, deno and uv run, as 108c4f4 chose; the lead may want to confirm that.

findings.how: In app/main/commands/classify.ts: (1) added a git `grep` verb handler (git(["grep"], ...)) that routes into the grep-family NATIVE handler as key "git-grep" (previously `grep` sat in GIT_READ and dropped its options). (2) In the grep-family handler, added longValue opts pager/filter/hostname-bin/open-files-in-pager and now classify each pager/filter value as the command it is: git grep -O<cmd>/--open-files-in-pager=<cmd>, ag/ack --pager, ugrep --pager and --filter (glob:cmd split) are nested as sh; a bare -O and rg --hostname-bin/--pre are unclear.rg-pre. (3) In the gdb/lldb handler, any of -ex/-iex/-x/-o/-O/-s/-S/--eval-command/--command/--source now yields unclear.inline-code, and batch mode runs only when none is present. | repair: Added debuggerCode() next to the gdb/lldb row and used it in place of the old regex. gdb: the option name is taken after one or two dashes and cut at `=`. It asks for ex, iex, x and ix, and for any prefix of 2 or more letters of eval-command, init-eval-command, command and init-command. gdb's -s (--symbols) no longer asks. lldb: asks for o, O, k, K, s and S, and for one-line, one-line-before-file, one-line-on-crash, source, source-before-file and source-on-crash, with one or two dashes. I checked the real tools here: `gdb -batch -ev 'shell echo'` ran the command, and so did `lldb -batch -one-line`; gdb refuses -in and -co as ambiguous. | repair: In the git-grep branch, the -O match is now /^-([A-Za-z0-9]*?)O(.*)$/. Every letter before O must be a flag that takes no value (not e, f, m, A, B or C). The text after O is the pager command and goes to h.e.nested; when it is empty, the case asks with unclear.rg-pre. One deviation from the suggested test: `git grep -iO'sh -c id' TODO` gives run, because the nested `sh -c id` is just `id`. That matches what `git grep -O'sh -c id'` already gave, so I used -iO'sh -c "rm -rf build"' as the ask case and kept -iO'sh -c id' as a run case. | repair: Fixed in the same commit. For git-grep and ugrep, `pager` and `open-files-in-pager` are no longer value options in the parse. Written alone they are flags, so the next word is the pattern or a file again, and only `=CMD` values reach h.e.nested. A bare `git grep --open-files-in-pager` asks with unclear.rg-pre, the same as a bare -O. ag and ack still take the next word as the pager. optIs is now imported from words.ts.

findings.how: Added a `stdinText` field to the Simple command (the visible text of a here-document/here-string on stdin: a here-string word, a quoted heredoc body, or an unquoted one with no expansions; null otherwise), computed via a new hereText() in posixSimple. Added a shared fromStdin(h, judge) helper: when the text is visible it calls judge, otherwise a preceding fetch is escape.download-run and anything else is unclear.stdin-code. Wired it into make/ninja (-f -, /dev/stdin, process substitution -> unclear.stdin-code), awk/gawk -f - (-> awkProgramOk), psql/sqlite3/sqlite/duckdb and mysql/mariadb when they read SQL from stdin (-> databaseText, i.e. the existing SQL_ESCAPE/SQL_WRITE checks), ed/ex scripts on stdin (a `!` shell escape -> unclear.ed-shell), and gdb -x /dev/stdin (covered by the gdb code-option check from #165). | repair: psql: when any -f/--file value is stdin (`-` or a STDIN_NAME), it now calls sqlFromStdin. sqlite3, sqlite and duckdb now handle -init/--init FILE: stdin goes to sqlFromStdin; any other file is judged with usePath(read) and asks with unclear.sql, as `.read` does. The values of -init and -cmd are no longer taken for the database or its SQL. One behaviour change: `sqlite3 -init x.sql x.db .tables` ran on the base and now asks (unclear.sql). This follows the suggested fix. | repair: Added STREAM_NAME, /^(\/dev\/fd\/\d+|\/proc\/(self|\d+)\/fd\/\d+)$/, and checked it after STDIN_NAME in make/gmake/ninja -f, awk -f, cmake -P, psql -f and sqlite3 -init. Such a stream asks with unclear.script-stream. The wording is the existing script-stream text, now kept in SAYS.scriptStream so every use of the rule says the same thing (the two old uses in recordScript use it too). | repair: Added a helper, sqlFromStdin, which calls fromStdin only when stdin is a here-document or a pipe. The mysql, psql and sqlite3 branches use it, so a file redirect (`psql < dump.sql`) runs as `psql -f dump.sql` does, as on 1b39bb3. Piped SQL still asks. | repair: Added edFiles(text, fileGiven), used in the ed/ex judge for text Ember can see. It reads each line after its address. e, E and r (ex: edit, read) read the file named. w, W, wq and x (ex: write, saveas, update) write it. A bare w writes the remembered name, which e, f, or a first r or w set when the command line named no file. Lines added with a, i or c up to a `.` line are skipped as text. A name starting with `!` stays the shell case. The case is now braced, because it declares a const.

findings.how: Download destinations. wget -P/--directory-prefix now judges the folder, a file in it, and folder/<name from the URL> as written (also the name in the current folder when there is no -P); an unseen -P or -O folder asks. aria2c judges -d/--dir as the folder, -o inside it, and -i as a read. axel --output and fetch -o are judged as written. lwp-download judges its second operand, and that operand plus the URL name. Folder judging uses only the path rules, so a script beside the download is still read first. git checkout-index got its own row: it judges <prefix><path> as written, and the prefix's folder when -a or --stdin is used; an unseen prefix asks. git worktree add judges its target folder and move its new folder. go build/test judges -o. The optionPaths pass also judges output long options (--output, --out, --output-file, --output-dir, --outdir, --outfile, --directory-prefix, --pack-destination) as written when the value looks like a path, so a format such as --output json or ps -o pid,comm is left alone. -o is judged the same way for unknown programs and for the known compilers and converters (gcc, cc, clang, ld, as, rustc, strip, pandoc), but stays a flag for read-only tools such as nm, strings and od. Those writes meet the start-up, autostart, system, secret and Ember rules only, so L8's rule about scripts this command writes is unchanged. The other programs in the finding's evidence are covered too: sponge, split and csplit (first output name), unrar (now uses rar's row), dpkg-deb -x/-X/-R, python -m zipfile/tarfile -e, cpio -D/--directory, pip download -d/-w, pip install --target/--root/--prefix/--src, and the file an ed or ex script edits. While writing the split row I also judge split --filter as nested shell text; that is a #165-type gap next to this step, not in its list. Ember's own settings: every listed form now refuses for ~/.config/ember. Not done here: ~/.local/bin is not yet a protected location, so wget -P ~/.local/bin and the verifier's gcc -o ~/.local/bin/ls still run. Step E (#172) adds .local/bin/ to the start-up list, and that makes them ask through this same code. The same command with ~/.bashrc asks now.

findings.how: In app/main/commands/classify.ts, containerRun now calls a new containerMounts(h, p) helper, and docker compose run -v calls it too. It reads every -v/--volume value and every --mount value. It handles host:container[:options] (a drive letter's colon is kept, and -v=x counts as -v x), --mount src=/source=, type=tmpfs, and readonly/ro (readonly=false means writable). The ro, readonly and podman O options count as read-only. Named volumes (a bare name such as data) and anonymous volumes (-v /x) are skipped. Every bind-mount host path is judged with usePath readTree and, unless read-only, also with write, so the secret, start-up, autostart, git-config, system and Ember rules all apply. The written list is restored afterwards, following the L8 'writes Ember doesn't follow' pattern. A mount of an engine socket or named pipe (*.sock, \\.\pipe\...), of a folder that holds one (/run, /var/run, /run/{docker,podman,containerd,crio,buildkit}, /run/user/<n>[/docker|podman|containerd]) or of a whole system folder (/usr /boot /sys /proc /dev /bin /sbin /lib* /etc /var /opt) asks as system docker.privileged, read-only or not. So does a writable mount under /sys/ or /proc/. A writable mount outside the task's folder (inWorkTree) asks as destroy docker.mount, 'Lets a container change or delete files in <path>.', following the archive.unpack precedent. A -v or --mount value Ember can't resolve asks as unclear.unresolved-arg. Before this, it was silently skipped. The two 'asks first' bullets in docs/COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md §2.4 now mention mounts. Behaviour change to note: -v $(pwd):/app now asks (unclear.unresolved-arg), as cat $(pwd)/x already did; "$PWD", ${PWD}, . and ./x still run. Not done (the reviewer called these optional): -u 0 / --user root, -p 0.0.0.0 and -e VAR=$SECRET. Also not done: an X11 socket mount (/tmp/.X11-unix), and judging the real path of a link inside the project for the work-tree test (archive.unpack does not do that either). | repair: posixWord now gives the scope's folder (as `$PWD` does) for a word whose only command substitution is a plain `pwd`: no arguments, redirections or assignments, exactly one sub and one command-substitution segment, so brace-expanded copies can't be mismatched. psArgValues does the same for a PowerShell value whose only subexpression is a plain Get-Location, pwd or gl. One round-2 fixture asserted that `docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/app alpine rm -rf /app/src` asks as unresolved. Its source is now $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel), which still can't be resolved, so it keeps testing what it was written for.

findings.how: In usePath (win32 flavour), a share path on another computer (\\host\... or //host/..., not WSL, a device or an admin share or localhost, which keep their rules) now gets a finding for every use, not only writes. Writes keep publish upload.unc. A program or script run from a share (exec, which covers program words, & / cmd /c / call / start / powershell -File / node and python scripts) gets escape escape.run-remote, 'Runs a program from another computer (<host>).'. Reads, listings and cd/pushd get publish net.unc, 'Connects to <host> and signs in there with your Windows account.'. The net handler now judges each \\host argument of net use, so net use [Z:] \\host\share asks. New-PSDrive (and its mount and ndr aliases) binds -Root, by name or by position, and judges a share root the same way before its non-Persist early return. Path inspection already skips UNC paths, so Ember itself never touches the share before asking. The 'publishes' and 'runs code' bullets in docs/COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md §2.4 now mention shares. One existing fixture changed on purpose: powershell.json 'New-PSDrive -Name X -PSProvider FileSystem -Root \\server\share' was run and is now ask (publish, net.unc), because it connects to that share exactly as net use does. A new case, New-PSDrive with root C:\Users\ana\proj, keeps the original intent covered: a session drive on a local folder still runs. | repair: In the powershell/pwsh native row, when the program is reached through WSL interop (h.pn.interop), the -File path is now also judged with usePath(file, "exec", child(h.sc, windowsScope(h, "powershell"))), before runScript. This gives escape.run-remote for \\host\share\… and //host/share/…. \\wsl.localhost and relative names still run. | repair: The net row now judges a \\host operand of `view` with usePath(list), as it already did for `use`. Added a CMDLETS row for resolve-path and convert-path. It binds -Path (positional) and -LiteralPath (aliases pspath, lp) and judges a \\ or // value with usePath(list). It still calls textProgram, so its checks for secret variables are kept; non-UNC paths give the same results as on the base.

findings.how: paths.ts: STARTUP_HOME gains .bashrc.d/ and .Xresources. AUTOSTART_HOME gains .local/share/applications/, .config/gnome-shell/ and .local/share/gnome-shell/extensions/. New BIN_HOME write kind (rule path.bin, system, "Changes which program a command name runs.") covers ~/.local/bin, ~/bin and Windows AppData/Local/Microsoft/WindowsApps, also under WSL's /mnt/c/Users/<u>. New PROGRAM_CONFIG_HOME write kind (rule path.program-config, system, "Changes what a program runs the next time you use it.") covers .vimrc, .gvimrc, .vim/, _vimrc, vimfiles/, .config/nvim/, AppData/Local/nvim/, .tmux.conf, .config/tmux/, .config/pip/, .pip/, AppData/Roaming/pip/, Library/Application Support/pip/, .cargo/config(.toml) and .m2/settings.xml. Both new kinds are wired into writeKind, the glob write entries, writeFinding and append(). Write kinds apply whether or not the file exists, so a new file there asks. classify.ts: a new desktop-file-install/desktop-file-edit/update-desktop-database row: --dir is judged with its default /usr/share/applications, edit is judged as a write, and update-desktop-database is judged as a write of mimeinfo.cache. "gio set … metadata::trusted <not false>" asks as system.security. The new names are in NOT_RUNNERS. docs/COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md lists the new system changes.
